title: Square coherence of the canonical coefficient pullback family
statement: For the same fixed B, eR, G, hG, let p be exactly the canonical family of [def-weil-pbc-canonical-finite-discrete-pullback]. For any commutative square sq:CommSq g′ f′ f g and K in D+ of etale B-module sheaves, F_X′(theta_etale(sq)_K) followed by p_g′ at f^*K and g′^*(p_f at K) equals p_f′ at g^*K followed by f′^*(p_g at K) and theta_internal(sq) at F_Y(K). Here theta_internal is coefficientAmbientSquare of [def-weil-pbc-coefficient-derived-functor-api]. No assertion is made about arbitrary choices of pullback isomorphisms.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.2 and Lemma 5.4.1; sectionwise coefficient encoding

proof.text: Use ordinary composition coherence of the specified sheaf comparison. Apply the proved mapDerivedCategorySquareIso_hom_app_comp theorem to the inverse comparisons and cancel their inverses to obtain exact-derived composition coherence.

Normalize the canonical derived coefficient comparison as realization_combine at the source, the exact-derived ordinary square, the inverse realization_combine at the target, and the exact-versus-left-derived inverse. Normalize leftDerivedUpperStarComp by its defining composition. Apply the elementary transport_comp calculation to naturality and exact-derived composition coherence; the intermediate realization and derived replacement isomorphisms cancel. The D+ composition map is the restriction of its full-derived counterpart.

For an arbitrary realization functor family and comparison family satisfying composition, compare the two composition equations. Equality elimination along the commutativity of the square identifies the canonical comparisons for the two composite scheme morphisms. Apply a generic categorical cancellation lemma, keeping both square comparison isomorphisms as parameters and identifying them with their specified three-factor compositions at the isomorphism level. This gives exactly the square equation, avoiding expansion of concrete derived-functor components.
